_comment: GENERATED from the git template named in `source` — do not hand-edit. Regenerate with `node scripts/template-parity-check.mjs --fix`; the gate fails when this file and its source disagree, so the guided form on the floor cannot drift from the artifact the gates read.
title: Business case
guidance: **Identifiers.** Gate ids (`D1`–`D9`) and run-level ids (`S-001` signal, `H1` hypothesis) are expanded in `discovery/GLOSSARY.md`. `SI-*` is a strategic intent from the institutional intake, where one exists.

properties.name: Run
properties.help: The discovery run this artifact belongs to.

sections.name: 1. The problem, and the intent it serves
sections.help: Quote, do not restate. The problem is frozen in `problem-statement.md`; a business case that re-frames it has left the run.

sections.name: 2. The case for acting, and the case for not
sections.help: **"Do nothing" is a mandatory row** — the cost of the problem continuing is the baseline every benefit is measured against, and it is the row most often left out. The other rows are *ways of framing the response*, not solution options: what is compared here is scope and timing, not mechanism. A row that names a technology, a vendor or a system design fails D4.
columns: What it means for the target user
Cost of this option, per year
Why it was set aside / kept

sections.name: 3. Benefits — the D1 success measures, valued
sections.help: **The rule that keeps this honest:** a benefit that is not a D1 success measure is not a benefit of *this* problem. Either it belongs in the problem statement (re-freeze the run) or it is dropped. The `product-eval-check` gate later scores every D1 measure against the shipping commit, so what is written here is what will be measured, by construction.
fields: Benefits finance does not count (ADOPT: from intake block H)
What the stakeholder reaction said about these (D9, stage 2)

sections.name: 4. Total cost of change
sections.help: A **band**, not a figure: discovery knows the shape of the change, not its build. One-off and recurring, separately. The build row is the one the Loom can later instrument (the token ledger, `token-report`); every other row is a human estimate and says so. **The rows most often under-counted are marked ▲.**

sections.name: 5. Financial summary *(stage 2)*
sections.help: Use the institution's mandated method (ADOPT: from intake block H). If there is none, say so and show payback only — do not invent a hurdle rate.

sections.name: 6. Risk and governance position
sections.help: Cite; do not re-assess. The positions below are held elsewhere and this case inherits them.
fields: Product approval (PA1/PA2), if compiled for this change
Assumptions that would change the answer

sections.name: 8. Benefits realisation
sections.help: Someone owns each measure after launch, and there is a date on which someone looks.
columns: Where the number will come from

sections.name: 9. Roster — who this goes to
sections.help: This table is the **roster**, not the approval. The decision is recorded in `decision_record` (front-matter) as an ADR or decision envelope merged by a human other than the proposer. Names resolve through `docs/governance/identities.json`; roles only here.
